description: Juniper EX2300-24P is a fixed 1RU Gigabit Ethernet access switch. It has 24 10/100/1000BASE-T ports, all with PoE+ and 370 W available, and four built-in 10-Gigabit SFP+/SFP uplink ports. The front carries the 24 jacks in two stacked rows numbered 0 to 23, and the upper jack of a column takes the even number. It also carries the four uplinks numbered 0 to 3, three status lamps, four port-mode lamps, a Factory Reset/Mode button and a mini-USB console port. The rear carries the management Ethernet port with a USB port under it, the RJ-45 console port, a two-hole earthing terminal and an ESD point. It also carries two exhaust fans and the AC power cord inlet. The power supply and both fans are built into the chassis, so there are no bays. The -TAA and -VC part numbers are the same chassis. The EX2300-24T is the same front without PoE.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Hardware guide, Power Supply in EX2300 Switches: "The power supply in EX2300 switches is built in along the rear panel of the chassis"; Table 34 lists "Switch with built-in power supply"; the cooling system is "two fans built-in along the rear of the chassis". Nothing in the guide describes removing or replacing either, and the guide's inventory example lists them as JPSU-450W-AC-AFO and Fan Module, Airflow Out (AFO) only as chassis items. They are part of the chassis, not bays and not components.

chassis.note: Table 3: height 1.75 in (4.45 cm), width 17.4 in (44.19 cm) and 19 in (48.26 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 12.2 in (30.98 cm) for models with PoE capability, weight 9.89 lb (4.49 kg). 441.9 x 44.45 x 309.8 is carried: the metric as printed for width and depth and the height as the 1U pitch Table 35 gives (1.75 in, 4.45 cm). The photographs show no ears, and the jack pitch closing on the registry at that width says the figure is the body.

colour.note: median of the bare front plate in the 24P photograph (#919599); the plate at the top right #6e7276.

front-console.note: estimated - the mini-USB console port (guide Figure 3, callout 5, printed CON) is drawn as chassis art, a 7.9 x 4.6 mm shell with its opening, read off the 24P and 48P photographs (25 x 14 px and 24 x 14 px at 3.27 px per mm). It is not a component: the library has no mini-USB receptacle and its DCIM export has no row for one, so a placed part would export nothing. The rear RJ-45 console port is a component and exports.

front-layout.note: estimated - read off the front photographs as described under gate-1. The 24 jacks stand in two shells of six columns, the first jack at 187.0 mm and the shell step 88.8 mm (6 x 13.97 plus a 5.0 gutter), right-aligned so that the last shell ends where the uplink block begins at 364.6; the rows are 14.8 mm apart and the upper row is turned 180 so its lamps and keyway are above, as the photograph shows. The four SFP+ cages abut on the registry pitch of 14.25 at 364.6, one row. A darker plate carries the model legend and lamps at the top right and runs down the far right edge. The hexagonal vent fields along the top edge and above the uplinks, and the slotted row along the bottom edge, are read off the same photographs.

gate-1.note: The 24P front photograph is 1500 x 190 px with the body 1446 px across and 143 down: 10.11 against the stated 441.9 / 44.45 = 9.94, 1.7 percent out, so x is taken at 3.272 px per mm from the width and y at 3.217 px per mm from the height. The ganged jack pitch then reads 45.7 px = 13.96 mm, the 0.550 in pitch the registry records for the ganged RJ-45 cell, on a quantity the scale never saw. The 48P photograph (1432 px across, 3.24 px per mm) agrees on every feature that both show to within 0.7 mm in x and 1.4 mm in y; the y values here are the mean of the two. Every position is therefore estimated and good to about a millimetre.

lamps.note: Hardware guide, Tables 4 to 12 and Figures 24, 26 and 27. Each RJ-45 port and uplink has two lamps, Link/Activity and Status; Figure 24 puts Link/Activity on one corner of the jack and Status on the other. The Status lamp reads out whichever of SPD, DX, EN and PoE the Factory Reset/Mode button has selected, shown by which port-mode lamp is lit. SYS is green, ALM red or yellow and MST green. The jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary because a block cannot override it per lamp. On the uplinks the left slot is taken as Link/Activity and the right as Status by analogy with the jacks, which no figure confirms, so it is estimated.

port-numbering.note: photo-measured - the photograph prints each column's two numbers in orange under the shell, the even number up and left and the odd number down and right (0 and 1, 2 and 3, ... 22 and 23), so the upper jack takes the even number; the uplinks print 0 to 3 in white between their two lamps. Port numbers are as printed on the metal, from 0. The Junos interface names are not printed: the guide's Table 2 gives PIC 0 as 24x10/100/1000 Base-T and PIC 1 as 4x10G SFP/SFP+, i.e. ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/23 and xe-0/1/0 to xe-0/1/3; they are recorded here and not in an interfaces block because the faceplate does not print them.

power.note: Table 14: maximum power consumed by the switch 80 W when no PoE power is drawn, maximum PoE/PoE+ power available 370 W; Table 15: 100 through 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 7 A at 100 VAC and 3.5 A at 240 VAC. The rear legend of the 48P photograph prints 12A Max, which is that model's Table 15 figure; the 24P's legend is drawn from Table 15 (7A) and not read off a figure.

rear-layout.note: estimated - positions off the 48P rear photograph (3.234 px per mm across, 3.09 px per mm down) for the management and console jacks, USB port, earthing terminal, ESD point, fans and AC inlet, which Figure 9 shows at the same places on the 24-port PoE model: the second fan sits at 0.78 of the width in Figure 9 (344.7 mm) where the 48P's sits next to the first. The guide's drawing puts a serial number label and a CLEI label on the rear; the studio photographs show neither, so none is drawn. The eight edge screws are read off Figure 9 (the body 874 px across at 1.978 px per mm, the first at 51.6 mm and the last at 424.7 mm, centres, drawn at y 37.4 as on the DC rear) and are estimated; no photograph of this rear is held, and the held NetBox 24T rear elevation shows the non-PoE rear, not this one.

sources.note: EX2300 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2025-08-12 (314 pages; https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex2300/ex2300.pdf): Figure 3 and Figure 4 (front panels), Figure 9 to Figure 13 (rear panels), Table 1 (models), Table 3 (chassis size and weight), Tables 4 to 12 (LEDs), the cooling system section, Tables 14 to 16 (power) and Table 34 (parts list). Juniper's own straight-on studio photographs of the EX2300-24P front (ex2300-24p-front-high.jpg), of the EX2300-48P front and rear, and of a DC-powered 24-port rear (file named ex2300-24p-rear-high.jpg, which shows the DC terminal block and a single fan, so it is the EX2300-24T-DC rear and not the 24P). The HPE PSNow datasheet (a00151236enw) did not answer when fetched, so no datasheet is cited. No studio photograph of the EX2300-24P rear exists in the maker's library; its rear is the 48P's photographed parts at the positions of the guide's Figure 9.
